viśāṃ pate = 'lord of the people'; प्रजापति in Hindi reads as the creator-god's name, which misleads.

The split satya-vāk + śūraḥ is right, but the printed kṣ (सत्यवाक्षूरो) for vāk + śūra is an orthographic rendering of k + ś (kś, optionally kch); the draft does not say so, and a reader may look for a word 'ṣūra'.

patch.text: satyavākṣūro = satyavāk + śūraḥ; the printed kṣ stands for the sandhi k + ś (kś / kch), as commonly written; not a typo.

summary: 42 units reviewed (P1, 1-41). 9 units need fixes; 1 error-severity issue (unit 22: upasevantu labelled middle, it is the active 3 pl. imperative) and 14 minor issues, nearly all small additions in the translations ('there' in 1 and 3, 'fruit of' in 12, 'all' in 16a, 'other'/अन्य in 24, यहाँ in 33, प्रजापति for viśāṃ pate in 34) plus two notes to append (22 kalyāṇam adverbial alternative; 36 kṣ for k+ś). Units 22 and 31 (medium confidence) were checked: 22's split and bahuvrīhi reading are sound and medium is honest given kalyāṇam's ambiguity; 31's reading of araṇīsahitasya arthe and dvaitavanaṃ prati is correct and medium confidence is appropriate since the line itself does not say what the test was. Unit 35a does repeat 11b verbatim; the Devanagari and IAST agree, nothing suggests a transcription slip, and the draft rightly keeps it with a note and no text_flag. The '~' candrabindu tokens in 10c and 23a are handled correctly. No regrouping suggested; all splits match the printed tokens. Glossary additions for GLOSSARY.md (reviewer to add): tāta = dear one (तात); nṛpa = O king (हे नृप); pārtha (voc.) = O Pārtha (हे पार्थ); mahābāho = mighty-armed one (हे महाबाहु); puruṣarṣabha = bull among men (हे पुरुषर्षभ); puruṣavyāghra / naraśārdūla = tiger among men (हे पुरुषव्याघ्र / हे नरशार्दूल); names: Śakra, Karṇa, Droṇa, Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī), Dharma (the god), Gaṅgā.
